catalog.detail: I want a plan for study and part-time work that I can actually keep up with, with some time left for music.

catalog.topic: Usual interests and hobbies, not current enjoyment
catalog.detail: Usually, I’ll put on a favorite album and listen to it all the way through.
A direct question works best for me. If it’s a big one, breaking it up helps.
I talk things through with my sibling when there’s a practical problem. With my friend, I’d rather make a plan than decide everything at the last minute.
Usually instrumental music or albums with a lot of guitar. I tend to play the tracks in order.

catalog.topic: Why listening to whole albums became a hobby
catalog.detail: I got curious about how the songs fit together. That’s why I started listening to whole albums instead of just individual tracks.

catalog.topic: Usual way of keeping study and work tasks visible
catalog.detail: I keep study tasks and work shifts on the same list, then mark what has a fixed time. I prefer seeing the commitments together before adding anything else.

catalog.topic: Earlier comparison of album opening tracks
catalog.detail: With a couple of albums I listened to before, I compared how their opening tracks led into the next song. I made a note about the order rather than rating every track.

catalog.topic: How Alex asks a sibling for practical help
catalog.detail: When I talk through a practical problem with my sibling, I usually show them the options I’ve already thought of and ask what I might have missed.

catalog.topic: Preference for plans that leave room around commitments
catalog.detail: I prefer making plans with a friend after checking my study and work commitments. I don’t want to agree to something and only then work out whether it fits.

catalog.topic: Usual way of dividing a study task
catalog.detail: For a study task, I usually write the next concrete step, such as opening the reading and choosing a section. A short next step is easier to plan around than the whole assignment.

catalog.topic: Wish for a future album conversation with a friend
catalog.detail: I’d like to pick an album with a friend and compare which track we think holds it together. We haven’t picked the album for that yet.
For four months, including the time before this diary, I have felt low and lost interest on most days. This is different from how I usually was before that period.
Sleep is broken, energy is low, concentrating takes effort and I am hard on myself. Activities I usually enjoy feel much less rewarding.
Everyday responsibilities take much longer, and I have pulled back from people and hobbies I care about.
I am in the young adult stage. My usual interests include listening to music. I want to take part in balancing study and part-time work, with support from my sibling.
